generation.forced_text:
Example prompt: How Does Mitotic DNA Seggregtion work to create two copies during division?
DNA is fundamental biological instruction code in nearly organisms' cell. Each human has ~ 2m copies total in every body part (though only some types like egg/s are haplogamous having single DNA code copies) spread in all cell’s 44 sets or diplocydes. Mitosis creates daughter nuclei containing an identital genetic makeup.

To accomplish identical copies:
First: The 890m nucleases enzymes chop up single strands to create replication initiation spots.
2) Single strand binds complementary DNA to make full copies
